title: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)
seoTitle: What Is RAG? Retrieval-Augmented Generation Explained
seoDescription: RAG lets an AI model answer from your own documents instead of memory. How it works, when to use it instead of fine-tuning, accuracy and costs.
summary: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is a way of making an AI model answer from your own documents: the system first finds the most relevant passages, then gives them to the model with the question, and the model answers using only that material, ideally citing where each point came from.

dataPoints.label: Typical sources
dataPoints.value: Manuals, policies, product catalogues, past proposals, SOPs, support tickets

dataPoints.label: Main benefit
dataPoints.value: Answers grounded in your material, updated as soon as documents change

dataPoints.label: Accuracy levers
dataPoints.value: Clean documents, good chunking, relevance ranking, citation checks

dataPoints.label: Typical pilot
dataPoints.value: 4–8 weeks on one document set and one user group

body:
## How RAG works

1. Documents are split into passages and indexed for search.
2. A question retrieves the most relevant passages.
3. The model answers from those passages and cites them.

## RAG or fine-tuning

Use RAG when answers must reflect current documents and be traceable. Fine-tuning changes how a model writes or classifies, not what it knows today. See [RAG or fine-tuning](/blog/rag-or-fine-tuning-choosing-the-right-approach-for-your-business-data).

## Where it fails

Poor or contradictory source documents, scanned files without text recognition, and questions the documents do not answer.

faqs.a: It reduces it a lot, especially with citations and instructions to say "I don't know", but outputs should still be checked for high-stakes uses.

faqs.q: Can RAG work with Hindi documents?
faqs.a: Yes, with models and search that handle Hindi well. Test on your real documents before committing.
